column1: # The arithmetic tables of the Metal backend: what each card's arithmetic can do, which arithmetic lane is wired into
# which kernel route, and which ops read a copy of their activations at the model's precision.
# A line that is exactly [name] starts a section; the next row is that section's header and is required as written.
# Cells are separated by one tab. - = absent. No file is read at run time: the generators below run when CMake configures.
# A card is named as Metal reports it, exactly: the text after "found device: " in the log of any run on that card (for
# example: AMD Radeon Pro Vega 64). A name that differs by one character matches no card.
# [capabilities]: what each card can do per arithmetic capability. lanes/gen-tables.cmake compiles the rows in
# (lanes-table.h, with [lanes]). ggml_metal_lane_ok_mask (lanes/select.cpp) turns the rows of one card into the set of
# capabilities it may use: a capability counts only when reached and correct are both yes. A card with no row can use
# the base lane of each route only. One row per card and capability.
# To add a row: run the lane probe on the card, or cite the document, and write where the cell values come from in source.
# In the three yes | no | unknown columns, unknown reads as no.
#   card: the card's name as Metal reports it (see above).
#   capability: the capability's name, the one a [lanes] row asks for in its capability column (for example pk-mul-f16, dot4-i32-i8). Lower-case letters, digits and -.
#   in_hardware: the chip has the instruction: yes | no | unknown. For the reader. The selector does not use it.
#   reached: the Metal shader compiler emits the instruction (seen as throughput in the probe): yes | no | unknown.
#   correct: the result equals the CPU reference: yes | no | unknown.
#   ratio: throughput against the fp32 lane on that card, a number above 0, or - when not timed. For the reader.
#   source: [capabilities]: where the cells come from: the probe and its date, or the document. Free text, no tab.
# [lanes]: which arithmetic lane is wired where. One row per (lane, family, route, operand types). lanes/gen-tables.cmake
# compiles the rows in (lanes-table.h). The selector, ggml_metal_negotiate_lane_in (lanes/select.cpp), reads only
# [lanes] and [capabilities]. It negotiates between the tensor type of the request (the model's requirement) and the
# card's capability rows: of the rows of the family and route that are on, it takes the one that holds the activation
# natively, else exactly another way, else wider. A row whose operand is narrower than the tensor is dropped. Equal
# steps go in file order, so the base row comes last. No row left = a coverage gap: the selector returns none.
# To add a lane: write its file, add its row with default off, run its test on the card, then turn it on.
#   lane: the lane's name, the same as its file name without the extension.
#   source ([lanes]): who compiles the lane: metal (the Metal shader compiler) | llvm-archive | llvm-native (LLVM). No llvm row exists yet.
#   file: the file that holds the lane, relative to this backend's folder. The table check fails when it does not exist.
#   family: the op family: matmul | flash-attn.
#   route: the route of the family: mv-scalar | mv-grouped | mm-tiled | mm-matrix | fa-scalar | fa-vec | fa-matrix | fa-intel-tiled.
#   weight: the weight type the row is for (a type name such as q4_K), or any = every type.
#   activation: the activation type the row is for (f32 | f16 | bf16), or any = every type.
#   operand: the format the lane holds an activation in while it forms products (f32 | f16 | bf16).

#   holds: how the operand holds the row's activation type: native | exact-other | wider | narrower. For activation any the request's type decides. The generator refuses a cell that contradicts operand and activation.
#   entry: the suffix of the lane's kernel entry point, or - = the route's own entry.
#   capability ([lanes]): the capability the card must have, a name of [capabilities], or - = none needed.
#   class: what the lane does to the values: exact | product-rounded | narrows.

#   origin: ours | upstream. upstream = a route that stages narrower types as shipped upstream. It is listed here and taken by its family's dispatch, not chosen by the selector, so it names no capability.
#   default: on | off. on = measured and reviewed, may be picked. off = the lane exists and is never picked.
#   seam_us: the cost in microseconds of handing the op to another submit route, 0 = none. A row with a cost is never picked.
#   id: the value of the pipeline lane constant, also part of the pipeline name. 0 for the base lane.
#   reason: [lanes]: why the row lands on its holds value. [copies]: why the row has its applies value (what was measured, or that nothing was). Free text, no tab.
#   test: [lanes]: the command that proves the row on a card before default is set to on. [copies]: the command that proves the row on the card before applies is set to yes. Free text, no tab.
# [copies]: which op families convert their activations once, at the start of the op, to the model's precision, per
# card. Tensors between ops stay f32. The copy is a scratch buffer owned by act-copy/. act-copy/gen-act-copy.cmake
# compiles the rows in (act-copy-table.h), and ggml_metal_act_copy_decide_in (act-copy/decide.cpp) picks the row of the
# op's card, family and route. A card with no row for a family and route gets no copy. One row per card, family, route and copy.
# To change a row: run its test on that card first, then set applies. A new family first needs a kernel entry that reads the copy's type.
#   card ([copies]): the card's name as Metal reports it (see above).
#   family ([copies]): the op family, as named in [lanes] (matmul | flash-attn).
#   route ([copies]): the route of that family whose kernel reads the copy, as named in [lanes] (for example mm-tiled).
#   copy: the type the activations are converted to: bf16 | f16. It applies only when it equals the model's precision.
#   applies: yes | no. no = the row is documented but the op reads its f32 activations as before.
#   min_rereads: the op must read each activation at least this many times, else no copy. A number from 4 (below 4 the conversion never pays).
#   max_bytes: the largest copy taken, in bytes. A larger activation is read as f32.
